nodes.title: About this template
widgets_values:
# 2 · YuE2 · Cover

**Source -> Transcribe Score -> Arrange -> Song Sheet · Score -> lyrics (ASR, writer or section tags) -> Song Sheet · Text -> YuE2 Takes -> Check Vocals -> Master -> Export**

1. Load the **source** recording (upload in *Load Audio*; up to 5:00 - trim longer songs with the optional *Excerpt* node).
2. In **Cover Brief** choose the **mode** - *new cover every run* (default): every run writes and renders a **different version** (title, style and - with new lyrics - the lyrics) without stops, so a queue of covers runs through; the batch count next to **Run** makes a series. Or *one cover, stop to review* (steps 4-6) to check the transcription and the lyrics first. Then the target style and what happens to the vocals: *original lyrics* (default; transcribed from the source), *instrumental* (an instrument plays the melody, or accompaniment only) or *new lyrics* (written on the source's melody). *harmony* keeps or replaces the original chords.
3. Press **Run**: SheetSage2 transcribes the source (once; later runs reuse it). With *new cover every run* the run goes on to the export.
4. With *one cover, stop to review* the run **stops at Song Sheet · Score**. Open it, check the score (fix section names and boundaries), then *Approve*.
5. Run again: the lyrics are drafted (ASR of the original, the writer's new lyrics, or the section tags) and the run **stops at Song Sheet · Text**. Correct or replace the lyrics - your text always wins - and *Approve*.
6. Run again to render. Each further run is a new take (the take seed changes).

**Original lyrics** are what *Transcribe Lyrics* hears in the source (Qwen3-ASR), placed into the score's sections. It hears the recording and the vocal stem *Sung Pitch* separates, and keeps the hearing it is more confident of - the stem only where it hears better (a separation also leaves artefacts that get misheard). **Fix Misheard Words** then has the writer model read them, with the words the ASR was unsure of marked, and correct the words it is sure were misheard - each with a word that sounds alike, fits the line and has as many syllables. Song Sheet · Text lists every correction beside the word heard; your text always wins. Only original lyrics are checked: new lyrics, an instrumental and lyrics you write yourself are never changed.

**New lyrics** are understood only when they fit the melody - about one syllable per note - and the voice fits its range; Song Sheet · Text warns about both.

**Creative modes (experimental):** *arrangement* in the brief. They can give unexpected results and are meant for experimenting - try a mode, listen, keep what you like. *off* (default, the dependable choice): no arrangement - the transcribed score stays as it is. A creative mode - from *standard*, *sterile* and *unplugged* over *call and response*, *signature motif*, *hypnotic* and *breakdown* to *jazz colours* and *fantasy* (the line under the brief says what the chosen one does), *key change* for one lift of the final chorus, or your own file in `user/plenio/arrangement` - adds its hints to the writing and lets the writer model plan every section of the score in **Arrange**: chords, what the instrument line plays, energy. *song flow closeness* sets how close it stays to the original: 100 exactly the original (no plan), 80 chords and key stay, 50 recognisable, 20 a free version, 0 only a hint - the form always remains, below 80 the melody follows the new chords. *lyrics closeness* (new lyrics) sets how close the new words stay to the source's: 0 without them (as before) up to 100, their meaning line by line. The writer answers with a small plan, never notes: Plenio writes every note itself and checks the result, so the score stays valid - a plan it cannot use leaves the score as it was, and Song Sheet · Score says so. A **harmony guard** keeps every chord in the key and the genre and on the melody, and the instrument line plays where the voice rests (*lines under the singing* in the brief lets it sound under the voice, calmly). **Arrangement seed:** another arrangement of the same song. Changing the mode or a slider writes the text again (the brief changed); a Local LLM answers from its cache when the request is the same.

**Writer model:** one list in the *Writer model* node - at the start, under the two cards - for every writing step (Write Song and Arrange): ComfyUI's text models (Gemma 4 E4B by default) and every local LLM - GGUF files in `models/LLM`, LM Studio, Ollama ... Only the chosen one is loaded. Local LLM answers are kept: the same request with the same seed is answered from Plenio's cache, without asking the model again.

**Where the run stands:** a badge above each Plenio node shows its result - ✓ done, ⚠ warning, ✖ error; every Song Sheet that will stop carries ⏸ *review stop* before the run, ⏸ *waiting for your approval* (and an amber frame) when the run stopped there, ✓ *approved* once you approved it. A new run clears the badges, so they show how far this run got.

**Creativity** (the brief's slider): 0 steady, 50 the reference - exactly as before -, 100 experimental. It shapes the writer's rules and the temperature of its draft (and of a creative mode's plan) and, with YuE2, how freely the plan and the takes are sampled. More surprises also bring more misses: try a few seeds. A workflow saved before the slider keeps 50.

**Lyrics fidelity** (the brief's last field): a music model does not always sing its lyrics - it leaves a line out, repeats one, sings other words. *standard* renders one take. *high - best of 2 takes* renders a second take (the next seed) when the first sang less than 96 % of the words as written, and **Best Take** keeps the one that sings more of the lyrics, as the lyrics ASR hears it; *highest - best of 3 takes* adds a third take when neither reached 96 %. A take of 96 % is close enough: the run goes on with it at once. Higher fidelity makes the generation take **longer** - up to about twice (high) or three times (highest). Best Take's summary and the release record say what each take sang and which one was kept.

**Seeds:** each seed node has one switch - **🔒 same seed**: the next run keeps that part (the same draft, the same take), so you can change other things; **🎲 new seed**: every run draws a new number - something new each time. The number shown is always the one the last run used: liked a take? Switch its seed to 🔒. Blue nodes keep, amber nodes renew. The seeds follow the brief's **mode**: *new song (cover) every run* starts with every seed on 🎲, *one song (cover), stop to review* with the song's seeds on 🔒 and the take seed on 🎲 - switching the mode switches them (a toast says so).

**Takes:** *YuE2 Takes* renders *takes* versions (seeds take seed, +1, ...); **Check Vocals** keeps the first instrumental take without vocal notes, the preview plays all takes. N takes cost N renders. **Instrumental adapter:** for instrumental covers YuE2 renders with the instrumental LoRA of the *Instrumental adapter* node (the optional adapter inside the model block stays bypassed here). **Check sung lyrics** (optional, bypassed) measures what a sung take actually sang.

**Finish:** *Plenio · Master* mixes the stems when you switch *stems* on, refines the take (*Audio HQ*, below) and brings it to -14 LUFS / -1 dBTP with a gentle tone match (open the block to change a stage, the EQ or the loudness target). Export writes the mastered FLAC 24-bit, the unmastered take as `(original).flac` and a release record to `output/plenio` - in the YuE2 templates also the **sheet music** with the lyrics as `<name>.pdf` (*sheet music* in Export: A4, Letter or off; *sheet music size*: standard about 3 bars a line, smaller, compact or large; this page draws it right after the export), and the lyrics as **subtitles** - `<name> (lines).srt` and `<name> (notes).srt`, timed by listening. The **tags** take the brief's fields as variables (`{genre}`, `{mood}` ...); the *Tags & variables* note beside Export lists them all.

**Cover art (on):** *Cover Art* (the COVER ART group above the render) paints a cover from the sheet's artwork prompt with FLUX.2 Klein 4B (about 16 GB of model files, Apache-2.0); Export embeds it in the FLAC and MP3 files and saves it as `.jpg`. The **Cover Art** card in *HQ Mastering & Cover Art* at the top switches it off - its three nodes are then bypassed and no image model loads.

**Stems (in the Master block, off):** switch *stems* on the *Plenio · Master* node on: *Separate Stems* splits the take into vocals, drums, bass and other, and the *Stem Mixer* - inside the block, open it with the icon at the top right of the node - balances them (gain, mute/solo, compression, reverb/delay sends, muted time ranges) and mixes the residual *rest* along, so a neutral mix returns the render unchanged. Off, the separation does not run. It needs the BS-RoFormer checkpoint (527 MB). The user guide *Stems* covers it.

**HQ Mastering & Cover Art** (the two cards at the top - click one to switch it): **HQ Mastering** (**off** by default) runs the mastering at its highest quality - it can clearly reduce AI shimmer and artifacts, but the song takes **about twice as long** (UniverSR, 229 MB in `models/audio_sr`, needed only then); **Cover Art** (**on**) paints the song's cover.

**Audio HQ (in the Master block, before the EQ):** *HQ 1 · Stereo Cleanup* calms the unsteady stereo shimmer in the render's highs (always); *HQ 2 · Regenerate Highs*, with HQ mastering on, lets the UniverSR model generate new highs above 8.2 kHz - in every preset - and blends them in at the original's level, about 1.5 s per second of music on an RTX 5060 Ti (its *model steps* 3: about 1.1 s); *HQ 3 · De-Reverb* (bypassed) dries the short metallic room but also dulls the highs. Their presets are on **auto**: the brief's genre picks *standard*, *gentle* (classical, jazz, folk), *strong* (rock, metal, punk) or *wide* (electronic, dance, ambient). Open the block (the icon at the top right of the node) to choose another preset or to bypass a stage (**Ctrl+B**). The user guide *Audio HQ* covers it.

**App mode:** switch *Graph / App* at the top left for a simple form: the source file, the mode, the cover style, the creative mode with both closeness sliders, the creativity, the writer model, the seeds, the two Song Sheet buttons (the review stops work in the app; their status line says where the run stands) and the results. The other options of *original lyrics* and *new lyrics* are set in the graph.

**Models:** every file, its folder and the files for a smaller or larger graphics card are in the note *Models · what goes where* on the left; ComfyUI offers the downloads when you open the template. The lyrics ASR (Qwen3-ASR 1.7B with Qwen3-ForcedAligner 0.6B, 4.1 + 1.8 GB; faster-whisper large-v3, 3.1 GB, only for a language the aligner does not know) is fetched by Plenio when first needed. YuE2, SheetSage2 and the adapter are **CC BY-NC 4.0 (non-commercial)**.

Modern dance-pop: four-on-the-floor kick, bright plucky synths, deep sidechained bass, claps, a tight pre-chorus build and an explosive chorus combining a sung hook with a post-chorus drop. Glossy radio production, huge and immediate.
[Genre: {genre} · ][Mood: {mood} · ][Language: {language} · ]Powered by Plenio Music Production System / ComfyUI

nodes.title: Tags & variables
widgets_values:
## Tags & variables

**Export Release** writes these tags into the FLAC and MP3 files. Every tag field takes text with
**variables** - or connect any text output to it (drag a link onto the field), such as a field of the brief.

- `{genre}` - the value of a variable
- `[Mood: {mood} · ]` - shown only when every variable inside has a value
- `{{` and `}}` - literal braces

**Song:** `{title}` `{lyrics}` `{style}` `{artwork_prompt}` `{duration}` `{bpm}` `{score_key}`

**Brief:** `{description}` `{template}` `{mode}` `{genre}` `{mood}` `{tempo}` `{length}` `{vocals}` `{language}` `{voice}` `{theme}` `{melody}` `{lead_instrument}` `{key}` `{meter}` `{arrangement}` `{genre_closeness}` `{lines_under_singing}` `{harmony}` `{song_flow_closeness}` `{lyrics_closeness}` `{creativity}`

**Run:** `{date}` `{year}` `{time}` `{seed}` `{take_seed}` `{draft_seed}` `{arrangement_seed}`

**Models:** `{model}` `{writer}` · **Plenio:** `{plenio_version}`

**Tags:** `{artist}` `{album}` `{album_artist}` `{composer}` `{track}` (in the file name and the other tags)

Examples - comment: `Genre: {genre}[, mood: {mood}][, sung in {language}]`; album: `{genre} Sessions {year}`;
file name: `{artist} - {title}`. A name that is no variable stops the run when you press **Run**, before
anything renders.

**Subtitles:** *lyrics subtitles (SRT)* (on) writes `<name> (lines).srt` - whole lines - and
`<name> (notes).srt` - the lines painted on note by note - next to the song, timed by listening: Qwen3-ASR
hears the words and Qwen3-ForcedAligner times them (4.1 + 1.8 GB, fetched on first use; faster-whisper for a
language the aligner does not know).

nodes.title: Models · what goes where
widgets_values:
# Models · what goes where

When the template opens, ComfyUI offers the files it misses (*Missing models*: download them there). By hand: put each file into its folder below - or into a folder of your `extra_model_paths.yaml`. **0 · System Check** lists what is there and what is missing.

## Needed
- [yue2_3b_int8_convrot.safetensors](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/YuE2/resolve/main/checkpoints/yue2_3b_int8_convrot.safetensors) · 4.0 GB · CC BY-NC 4.0  
  YuE2 3B music model (int8)
- [ar_lora_inst_v3abc_comfyui.safetensors](https://huggingface.co/Mothersuperior/YuE2-instrumental-cot-full-loras/resolve/947f2f4b28978b2b6c3e316e6a87925c76bf3c4b/ar_lora_inst_v3abc_comfyui.safetensors) · see the model card · CC BY-NC 4.0  
  YuE2 instrumental adapter (community LoRA)
- [sheetsage2_bf16.safetensors](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/YuE2/resolve/main/audio_encoders/sheetsage2_bf16.safetensors) · 1.4 GB · CC BY-NC 4.0  
  SheetSage2 transcription (score of the source, Check Vocals)
- [gemma4_e4b_it_fp8_scaled.safetensors](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/gemma-4/resolve/main/text_encoders/gemma4_e4b_it_fp8_scaled.safetensors) · see the model card · Apache-2.0  
  Gemma 4 E4B writer (title, style or caption, lyrics, artwork prompt)
- [flux-2-klein-4b.safetensors](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/flux2-klein/resolve/main/split_files/diffusion_models/flux-2-klein-4b.safetensors) · 7.8 GB · Apache-2.0  
  FLUX.2 Klein 4B image model (distilled, cover art)
- [qwen_3_4b.safetensors](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/flux2-klein/resolve/main/split_files/text_encoders/qwen_3_4b.safetensors) · 8.0 GB · Apache-2.0  
  Qwen3 4B text encoder of FLUX.2 Klein
- [flux2-vae.safetensors](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/flux2-dev/resolve/main/split_files/vae/flux2-vae.safetensors) · 336 MB · Apache-2.0  
  FLUX.2 image VAE

## Optional
- [pytorch_model.bin](https://huggingface.co/woongzip1/universr-audio/resolve/main/pytorch_model.bin) · 229 MB · CC BY 4.0 (weights); MIT (inference code)  
  HQ mastering (the *HQ Mastering* card): UniverSR regenerates the highs above 8.2 kHz
- [model_bs_roformer_ep_17_sdr_9.6568.ckpt](https://github.com/ZFTurbo/Music-Source-Separation-Training/releases/download/v1.0.12/model_bs_roformer_ep_17_sdr_9.6568.ckpt) · 527 MB · MIT (trainer); trained on MUSDB18-HQ, whose dataset terms are research-oriented  
  stems (the Master's *stems* switch); when it is there, Export Release also hears the lyrics on the vocal stem - their times get more exact

## Where they go

```
📂 ComfyUI/
└── 📂 models/
    ├── 📂 audio_encoders/
    │   └── sheetsage2_bf16.safetensors
    ├── 📂 audio_separation/ (stems, the vocal stem for the lyrics times)
    │   └── model_bs_roformer_ep_17_sdr_9.6568.ckpt
    ├── 📂 audio_sr/ (HQ mastering)
    │   └── pytorch_model.bin
    ├── 📂 checkpoints/
    │   └── yue2_3b_int8_convrot.safetensors
    ├── 📂 diffusion_models/
    │   └── flux-2-klein-4b.safetensors
    ├── 📂 loras/
    │   └── ar_lora_inst_v3abc_comfyui.safetensors
    ├── 📂 text_encoders/
    │   ├── gemma4_e4b_it_fp8_scaled.safetensors
    │   └── qwen_3_4b.safetensors
    ├── 📂 vae/
    │   └── flux2-vae.safetensors
    └── 📂 plenio/asr/ (Plenio fetches these)
        ├── qwen3-asr-1.7b-hf/
        └── qwen3-forcedaligner-0.6b-hf/
```

The lyrics ASR (Qwen3-ASR 1.7B, 4.1 GB, and its aligner, 1.8 GB) times the lyrics subtitles and hears a cover's words: Plenio downloads it into `models/plenio/asr` the first time it is needed. Offline (`PLENIO_OFFLINE=1`) it names the files to place.

**The writer** can also be a GGUF file of your own in `models/LLM` (or LM Studio's folder) or a model of a running LM Studio, Ollama, llama.cpp, vLLM or Jan: choose it in *Writer model*. Only the one chosen is loaded.

## Your graphics card

| Graphics card | Music model | Cover Art |
|---|---|---|
| below 8 GB | only with heavy offloading (the int8 model alone is 4 GB): very slow, keep songs short | not practical |
| 8-12 GB | int8 checkpoint (template default); keep songs short | choose `flux-2-klein-4b-fp8` and the text encoder `qwen_3_4b_fp4_flux2` |
| 12-16 GB | int8 checkpoint (template default) | fp8 model and fp4 text encoder |
| 16-24 GB | int8 checkpoint (template default) with the Gemma 4 E4B writer | template defaults (bf16) |
| 24 GB and more | the bf16 checkpoint `yue2_3b_bf16` (7.8 GB) is possible; int8 stays the faster default | template defaults |

No graphics card: the music models are not practical on the CPU; 0 · System Check and 4 · Enhance & Master run on it.

**Files for another card** (choose them in the loader nodes - nothing is switched by itself):
- instead of `yue2_3b_int8_convrot.safetensors`: [yue2_3b_bf16.safetensors](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/YuE2/resolve/main/checkpoints/yue2_3b_bf16.safetensors) · 7.8 GB · `checkpoints/`
- instead of `flux-2-klein-4b.safetensors`: [flux-2-klein-4b-fp8.safetensors](https://huggingface.co/black-forest-labs/FLUX.2-klein-4b-fp8/resolve/5b4408e59397a4a37ccb46afe426d8ed86379441/flux-2-klein-4b-fp8.safetensors) · 4.1 GB · `diffusion_models/`
- instead of `qwen_3_4b.safetensors`: [qwen_3_4b_fp4_flux2.safetensors](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/vae-text-encorder-for-flux-klein-4b/resolve/5f526678002e43af5551dadb73ce2e8c91b43afe/split_files/text_encoders/qwen_3_4b_fp4_flux2.safetensors) · 3.8 GB · `text_encoders/`

Licences: [docs/user/licensing.md](https://github.com/jplenio/Plenio-Music-Production-System/blob/main/docs/user/licensing.md) · every file: [docs/user/models.md](https://github.com/jplenio/Plenio-Music-Production-System/blob/main/docs/user/models.md)

subgraphs.name: Plenio · YuE2 Model
subgraphs.description: Loads YuE2 (int8 by default) and identifies it for the Plenio nodes. Contains an optional instrumental adapter (LoRA, CC BY-NC 4.0), bypassed by default.

subgraphs.name: Plenio · Write Song
subgraphs.description: Writes title, style, lyrics and an artwork prompt following the rules of the loaded music model. The writer model is one list: ComfyUI's own text models (native Generate Text, the default) and every local LLM - GGUF files from models/LLM, LM Studio or the Hugging Face cache, or the models of a running LM Studio, Ollama, llama.cpp ... Only the chosen one is loaded. The brief's song seed is added to the draft seed: every song of a 'new song every run' series gets its own. New cover lyrics are fitted to the melody: lines that do not fit their phrase go back to the same writer, only those lines and at most twice (Fit Lyrics); when the draft fits, no second writer call is made.

subgraphs.name: Plenio · Transcribe Score
subgraphs.description: Transcribes a recording into a native two-voice ABC score with SheetSage2 and keeps the beat grid (bar times, sung notes) for lyrics alignment. Also outputs the loaded SheetSage2 for Check Vocals. SheetSage2 weights are CC BY-NC 4.0.

subgraphs.name: Plenio · Arrange
subgraphs.description: The creative modes' section plan: the writer model plans every section of the score (chords, what the instrument line plays, energy; a key change only in the mode key change) as a small JSON plan, and Plenio writes the notes and checks the result - or keeps the score as it was and says why (in the report and the Song Sheet). In the brief's arrangement off nothing runs here. The writer model is the same list as Write Song's; GGUF files, LM Studio and Ollama keep to the plan's format exactly. The arrangement seed gives another arrangement of the same song. Sections whose chords the harmony check had to repair much go back to the writer once (the re-ask); the better arrangement is used.

subgraphs.name: Plenio · Fix Misheard Words
subgraphs.description: Misheard words in a cover's original lyrics, before the render: the writer model reads the lyrics Transcribe Lyrics heard in the source, with the words it was unsure of marked, and corrects those it is sure were misheard - with a word that sounds alike, fits the line and has as many syllables. The Song Sheet lists each correction with the word heard. Only a Cover Brief with original lyrics asks the writer; new lyrics, an instrumental and lyrics you write yourself are never changed.

subgraphs.name: Plenio · YuE2 Takes
subgraphs.description: Renders the final style, lyrics and score N times with the seeds take seed, take seed + 1, ... (native loop). Connect the takes to Check Vocals, which keeps the best one. N takes cost N renders. Two more takes (the seeds after them) render only when Best Take asks for them (the brief's lyrics fidelity).

subgraphs.name: Plenio · Master

nodes.title: Stems on: the mix · off: the song

subgraphs.description: Finishes a song: Stems (with the block's stems switch on: Separate Stems and the Stem Mixer, set the mix inside the block) - Audio HQ: HQ 1 · Stereo Cleanup runs, HQ 2 · Regenerate Highs (UniverSR) with HQ mastering on (fewer AI shimmer and artifacts, about twice the time), HQ 3 · De-Reverb is bypassed; their presets follow the brief's genre - then a gentle tone match (EQ) and loudness for streaming (-14 LUFS, -1 dBTP true peak) with gentle compression. Open the block to mix the stems, change a preset, bypass a stage (Ctrl+B), the EQ curve or the compression style.

subgraphs.name: Plenio · Cover Art
subgraphs.description: Paints the cover from the Song Sheet's artwork prompt with FLUX.2 Klein 4B (distilled, 4 steps, native nodes; Apache-2.0). On in the song templates (about 16 GB of model files): the Cover Art card of HQ Mastering & Cover Art switches it off. The writer's artwork prompt is read from the song - its lyrics, its title, its genre and mood. The seed decides the picture; another seed, another cover. Replace the block with any text-to-image block that takes a prompt and gives an image.
